# frame_system - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/frame-system/48.0.0/frame_system/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#system-pallet)System Pallet

The System pallet provides low-level access to core types and cross-cutting utilities. It acts as the base layer for other pallets to interact with the Substrate framework components.

[§](https://docs.rs#overview)Overview

The System pallet defines the core data types used in a Substrate runtime. It also provides
several utility functions (see [ Pallet](https://docs.rs/pallet/struct.Pallet.html)) for other FRAME pallets.

In addition, it manages the storage items for extrinsic data, indices, event records, and digest items, among other things that support the execution of the current block.

It also handles low-level tasks like depositing logs, basic set up and take down of temporary storage entries, and access to previous block hashes.

[§](https://docs.rs#interface)Interface

[§](https://docs.rs#dispatchable-functions)Dispatchable Functions

The System pallet provides dispatchable functions that, with the exception of `remark`, manage
low-level or privileged functionality of a Substrate-based runtime.

- `remark`: Make some on-chain remark.
- `set_heap_pages`: Set the number of pages in the WebAssembly environment’s heap.
- `set_code`: Set the new runtime code.
- `set_code_without_checks`: Set the new runtime code without any checks.
- `set_storage`: Set some items of storage.
- `kill_storage`: Kill some items from storage.
- `kill_prefix`: Kill all storage items with a key that starts with the given prefix.
- `remark_with_event`: Make some on-chain remark and emit an event.
- `do_task`: Do some specified task.
- `authorize_upgrade`: Authorize new runtime code.
- `authorize_upgrade_without_checks`: Authorize new runtime code and an upgrade sans verification.
- `apply_authorized_upgrade`: Provide new, already-authorized runtime code.

[§](https://docs.rs#a-note-on-upgrades)A Note on Upgrades

The pallet provides two primary means of upgrading the runtime, a single-phase means using
`set_code` and a two-phase means using `authorize_upgrade` followed by
`apply_authorized_upgrade`. The first will directly attempt to apply the provided `code`
(application may have to be scheduled, depending on the context and implementation of the
`OnSetCode` trait).

The `authorize_upgrade` route allows the authorization of a runtime’s code hash. Once
authorized, anyone may upload the correct runtime to apply the code. This pattern is useful when
providing the runtime ahead of time may be unwieldy, for example when a large preimage (the
code) would need to be stored on-chain or sent over a message transport protocol such as a
bridge.

The `*_without_checks` variants do not perform any version checks, so using them runs the risk
of applying a downgrade or entirely other chain specification. They will still validate that the
`code` meets the authorized hash.

[§](https://docs.rs#public-functions)Public Functions

See the [ Pallet](https://docs.rs/pallet/struct.Pallet.html) struct for details of publicly available functions.

[§](https://docs.rs#signed-extensions)Signed Extensions

The System pallet defines the following extensions:

- `CheckWeight`
- `CheckNonce`- `T::Nonce`.
- `CheckEra`- `Era`.
- `CheckGenesis`
- `CheckSpecVersion`
- `CheckTxVersion`

Look up the runtime aggregator file (e.g. `node/runtime`) to see the full list of signed
extensions included in a chain.

- Returns a 32 byte datum which is guaranteed to be universally unique. `entropy`is provided as a facility to reduce the potential for precalculating results.

- An object to track the currently used extrinsic weight in a block.

- Type used to encode the number of references an account has.

# rust-url

URL library for Rust, based on the [URL Standard](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/).

Please see [UPGRADING.md](https://github.com/servo/rust-url/blob/main/UPGRADING.md) if you are upgrading from a previous version.

## Alternative Unicode back ends

`url` depends on the `idna` crate. By default, `idna` uses [ICU4X](https://github.com/unicode-org/icu4x/) as its Unicode back end. If you wish to opt for different tradeoffs between correctness, run-time performance, binary size, compile time, and MSRV, please see the [README of the latest version of the  idna_adapter crate](https://docs.rs/crate/idna_adapter/latest) for how to opt into a different Unicode back end.

# url - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/url/2.5.8/target-redirect/url/

## Expand description

rust-url is an implementation of the [URL Standard](http://url.spec.whatwg.org/)
for the [Rust](http://rust-lang.org/) programming language.

[§](https://docs.rs#url-parsing-and-data-structures)URL parsing and data structures

First, URL parsing may fail for various reasons and therefore returns a `Result`.

```
use url::{Url, ParseError};
assert!(Url::parse("http://[:::1]") == Err(ParseError::InvalidIpv6Address))
```
Let’s parse a valid URL and look at its components.

```
use url::{Url, Host, Position};
let issue_list_url = Url::parse(
    "https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues?labels=E-easy&state=open"
)?;
assert!(issue_list_url.scheme() == "https");
assert!(issue_list_url.username() == "");
assert!(issue_list_url.password() == None);
assert!(issue_list_url.host_str() == Some("github.com"));
assert!(issue_list_url.host() == Some(Host::Domain("github.com")));
assert!(issue_list_url.port() == None);
assert!(issue_list_url.path() == "/rust-lang/rust/issues");
assert!(issue_list_url.path_segments().map(|c| c.collect::<Vec<_>>()) ==
        Some(vec!["rust-lang", "rust", "issues"]));
assert!(issue_list_url.query() == Some("labels=E-easy&state=open"));
assert!(&issue_list_url[Position::BeforePath..] == "/rust-lang/rust/issues?labels=E-easy&state=open");
assert!(issue_list_url.fragment() == None);
assert!(!issue_list_url.cannot_be_a_base());
```
Some URLs are said to be *cannot-be-a-base*:
they don’t have a username, password, host, or port,
and their “path” is an arbitrary string rather than slash-separated segments:

```
use url::Url;
let data_url = Url::parse("data:text/plain,Hello?World#")?;
assert!(data_url.cannot_be_a_base());
assert!(data_url.scheme() == "data");
assert!(data_url.path() == "text/plain,Hello");
assert!(data_url.path_segments().is_none());
assert!(data_url.query() == Some("World"));
assert!(data_url.fragment() == Some(""));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#default-features)Default Features

Versions `<= 2.5.2` of the crate have no default features. Versions `> 2.5.2` have the default feature ‘std’.
If you are upgrading across this boundary and you have specified `default-features = false`, then
you will need to add the ‘std’ feature or the ‘alloc’ feature to your dependency.
The ‘std’ feature has the same behavior as the previous versions. The ‘alloc’ feature
provides no_std support.

[§](https://docs.rs#serde)Serde

Enable the `serde` feature to include `Deserialize` and `Serialize` implementations for `url::Url`.

[§](https://docs.rs#base-url)Base URL

Many contexts allow URL *references* that can be relative to a *base URL*:

`<link rel="stylesheet" href="../main.css">`Since parsed URLs are absolute, giving a base is required for parsing relative URLs:

```
use url::{Url, ParseError};
assert!(Url::parse("../main.css") == Err(ParseError::RelativeUrlWithoutBase))
```
Use the `join` method on an `Url` to use it as a base URL:

```
use url::Url;
let this_document = Url::parse("http://servo.github.io/rust-url/url/index.html")?;
let css_url = this_document.join("../main.css")?;
assert_eq!(css_url.as_str(), "http://servo.github.io/rust-url/main.css");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#feature-serde)Feature: `serde`

If you enable the `serde` feature, [ Url](https://docs.rs/struct.Url.html) will implement

[and](https://docs.rs/serde/1/serde/trait.Serialize.html)

`serde::Serialize`[. See](https://docs.rs/serde/1/serde/trait.Deserialize.html)

`serde::Deserialize`[serde documentation](https://serde.rs)for more information.

`url = { version = "2", features = ["serde"] }`[§](https://docs.rs#feature-debugger_visualizer)Feature: `debugger_visualizer`

If you enable the `debugger_visualizer` feature, the `url` crate will include
a [natvis file](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/visualstudio/debugger/create-custom-views-of-native-objects)
for [Visual Studio](https://www.visualstudio.com/) that allows you to view
[ Url](https://docs.rs/struct.Url.html) objects in the debugger.

This feature requires Rust 1.71 or later.

`url = { version = "2", features = ["debugger_visualizer"] }`## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use`- [form_urlencoded](https://docs.rs/form_urlencoded/1.2.2/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/form_urlencoded/index.html);

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Opaque](https://docs.rs/struct.OpaqueOrigin.html)- Origin
- Opaque identifier for URLs that have file or other schemes
- [Parse](https://docs.rs/struct.ParseOptions.html)- Options
- Full configuration for the URL parser.
- [Path](https://docs.rs/struct.PathSegmentsMut.html)- Segments - Mut
- Exposes methods to manipulate the path of an URL that is not cannot-be-base.
- [Url](https://docs.rs/struct.Url.html)
- A parsed URL record.
- [UrlQuery](https://docs.rs/struct.UrlQuery.html)
- Implementation detail of `Url::query_pairs_mut`. Typically not used directly.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Host](https://docs.rs/enum.Host.html)
- The host name of an URL.
- [Origin](https://docs.rs/enum.Origin.html)
- The origin of an URL
- [Parse](https://docs.rs/enum.ParseError.html)- Error
- Errors that can occur during parsing.
- [Position](https://docs.rs/enum.Position.html)
- Indicates a position within a URL based on its components.
- [Syntax](https://docs.rs/enum.SyntaxViolation.html)- Violation
- Non-fatal syntax violations that can occur during parsing.

[229](https://docs.rs#229)    /// Syntax in pseudo-BNF:
[230](https://docs.rs#230)    ///
[231](https://docs.rs#231)    ///   url = scheme ":" [ hierarchical | non-hierarchical ] [ "?" query ]? [ "#" fragment ]?
[232](https://docs.rs#232)    ///   non-hierarchical = non-hierarchical-path
[233](https://docs.rs#233)    ///   non-hierarchical-path = /* Does not start with "/" */
[234](https://docs.rs#234)    ///   hierarchical = authority? hierarchical-path
[235](https://docs.rs#235)    ///   authority = "//" userinfo? host [ ":" port ]?
[236](https://docs.rs#236)    ///   userinfo = username [ ":" password ]? "@"
[237](https://docs.rs#237)    ///   hierarchical-path = [ "/" path-segment ]+
[238](https://docs.rs#238)    serialization: [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html),
[239](https://docs.rs#239)
[240](https://docs.rs#240)    // Components
[241](https://docs.rs#241)    scheme_end: [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html),   // Before ':'
[242](https://docs.rs#242)    username_end: [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html), // Before ':' (if a password is given) or '@' (if not)
[243](https://docs.rs#243)    host_start: [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html),
[244](https://docs.rs#244)    host_end: [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html),
[245](https://docs.rs#245)    host: [HostInternal](https://docs.rs/host.rs.html#25-30),
[246](https://docs.rs#246)    port: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[u16](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u16.html)>,
[247](https://docs.rs#247)    path_start: [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html),             // Before initial '/', if any
[248](https://docs.rs#248)    query_start: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)>,    // Before '?', unlike Position::QueryStart
[249](https://docs.rs#249)    fragment_start: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)>, // Before '#', unlike Position::FragmentStart

[290](https://docs.rs#290)    /// let url = Url::options()
[291](https://docs.rs#291)    ///     .syntax_violation_callback(Some(&|v| violations.borrow_mut().push(v)))
[292](https://docs.rs#292)    ///     .parse("https:////example.com")?;
[293](https://docs.rs#293)    /// assert_eq!(url.as_str(), "https://example.com/");
[294](https://docs.rs#294)    /// assert_eq!(violations.into_inner(),
[295](https://docs.rs#295)    ///            vec!(SyntaxViolation::ExpectedDoubleSlash));
[296](https://docs.rs#296)    /// # Ok(())
[297](https://docs.rs#297)    /// # }

[299](https://docs.rs#299)    /// ```

[412](https://docs.rs#412)
[413](https://docs.rs#413)    /// Parse a string as an URL, with this URL as the base URL.
[414](https://docs.rs#414)    ///
[415](https://docs.rs#415)    /// The inverse of this is [`make_relative`].
[416](https://docs.rs#416)    ///
[417](https://docs.rs#417)    /// # Notes
[418](https://docs.rs#418)    ///
[419](https://docs.rs#419)    /// - A trailing slash is significant.
[420](https://docs.rs#420)    ///   Without it, the last path component is considered to be a “file” name
[421](https://docs.rs#421)    ///   to be removed to get at the “directory” that is used as the base.
[422](https://docs.rs#422)    /// - A [scheme relative special URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#scheme-relative-special-url-string)
[423](https://docs.rs#423)    ///   as input replaces everything in the base URL after the scheme.
[424](https://docs.rs#424)    /// - An absolute URL (with a scheme) as input replaces the whole base URL (even the scheme).
[425](https://docs.rs#425)    ///
[426](https://docs.rs#426)    /// # Examples
[427](https://docs.rs#427)    ///
[428](https://docs.rs#428)    /// ```rust
[429](https://docs.rs#429)    /// use url::Url;
[430](https://docs.rs#430)    /// # use url::ParseError;
[431](https://docs.rs#431)    ///
[432](https://docs.rs#432)    /// // Base without a trailing slash
[433](https://docs.rs#433)    /// # fn run() -> Result<(), ParseError> {
[434](https://docs.rs#434)    /// let base = Url::parse("https://example.net/a/b.html")?;
[435](https://docs.rs#435)    /// let url = base.join("c.png")?;
[436](https://docs.rs#436)    /// assert_eq!(url.as_str(), "https://example.net/a/c.png");  // Not /a/b.html/c.png
[437](https://docs.rs#437)    ///
[438](https://docs.rs#438)    /// // Base with a trailing slash
[439](https://docs.rs#439)    /// let base = Url::parse("https://example.net/a/b/")?;
[440](https://docs.rs#440)    /// let url = base.join("c.png")?;
[441](https://docs.rs#441)    /// assert_eq!(url.as_str(), "https://example.net/a/b/c.png");
[442](https://docs.rs#442)    ///
[443](https://docs.rs#443)    /// // Input as scheme relative special URL
[444](https://docs.rs#444)    /// let base = Url::parse("https://alice.com/a")?;
[445](https://docs.rs#445)    /// let url = base.join("//eve.com/b")?;
[446](https://docs.rs#446)    /// assert_eq!(url.as_str(), "https://eve.com/b");
[447](https://docs.rs#447)    ///
[448](https://docs.rs#448)    /// // Input as base url relative special URL
[449](https://docs.rs#449)    /// let base = Url::parse("https://alice.com/a")?;
[450](https://docs.rs#450)    /// let url = base.join("/v1/meta")?;
[451](https://docs.rs#451)    /// assert_eq!(url.as_str(), "https://alice.com/v1/meta");
[452](https://docs.rs#452)    ///
[453](https://docs.rs#453)    /// // Input as absolute URL
[454](https://docs.rs#454)    /// let base = Url::parse("https://alice.com/a")?;
[455](https://docs.rs#455)    /// let url = base.join("http://eve.com/b")?;
[456](https://docs.rs#456)    /// assert_eq!(url.as_str(), "http://eve.com/b");  // http instead of https
[457](https://docs.rs#457)    ///
[458](https://docs.rs#458)    /// # Ok(())
[459](https://docs.rs#459)    /// # }
[460](https://docs.rs#460)    /// # run().unwrap();
[461](https://docs.rs#461)    /// ```
[462](https://docs.rs#462)    ///
[463](https://docs.rs#463)    /// # Errors
[464](https://docs.rs#464)    ///
[465](https://docs.rs#465)    /// If the function can not parse an URL from the given string
[466](https://docs.rs#466)    /// with this URL as the base URL, a [`ParseError`] variant will be returned.
[467](https://docs.rs#467)    ///
[468](https://docs.rs#468)    /// [`ParseError`]: enum.ParseError.html
[469](https://docs.rs#469)    /// [`make_relative`]: #method.make_relative
[470](https://docs.rs#470)    #[inline]
[471](https://docs.rs#471)    pub fn join(&self, input: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<Self, crate::[ParseError](https://docs.rs/parser.rs.html#88-99)> {
[472](https://docs.rs#472)        Self::[options](https://docs.rs#626-632)().[base_url](https://docs.rs#266-269)([Some](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.Some)([self](https://docs.rs#471))).[parse](https://docs.rs#306-315)([input](https://docs.rs#471))
[473](https://docs.rs#473)    }
[474](https://docs.rs#474)
[475](https://docs.rs#475)    /// Creates a relative URL if possible, with this URL as the base URL.
[476](https://docs.rs#476)    ///
[477](https://docs.rs#477)    /// This is the inverse of [`join`].
[478](https://docs.rs#478)    ///
[479](https://docs.rs#479)    /// # Examples
[480](https://docs.rs#480)    ///
[481](https://docs.rs#481)    /// ```rust
[482](https://docs.rs#482)    /// use url::Url;
[483](https://docs.rs#483)    /// # use url::ParseError;
[484](https://docs.rs#484)    ///
[485](https://docs.rs#485)    /// # fn run() -> Result<(), ParseError> {
[486](https://docs.rs#486)    /// let base = Url::parse("https://example.net/a/b.html")?;
[487](https://docs.rs#487)    /// let url = Url::parse("https://example.net/a/c.png")?;
[488](https://docs.rs#488)    /// let relative = base.make_relative(&url);
[489](https://docs.rs#489)    /// assert_eq!(relative.as_ref().map(|s| s.as_str()), Some("c.png"));
[490](https://docs.rs#490)    ///
[491](https://docs.rs#491)    /// let base = Url::parse("https://example.net/a/b/")?;
[492](https://docs.rs#492)    /// let url = Url::parse("https://example.net/a/b/c.png")?;
[493](https://docs.rs#493)    /// let relative = base.make_relative(&url);
[494](https://docs.rs#494)    /// assert_eq!(relative.as_ref().map(|s| s.as_str()), Some("c.png"));
[495](https://docs.rs#495)    ///
[496](https://docs.rs#496)    /// let base = Url::parse("https://example.net/a/b/")?;
[497](https://docs.rs#497)    /// let url = Url::parse("https://example.net/a/d/c.png")?;
[498](https://docs.rs#498)    /// let relative = base.make_relative(&url);
[499](https://docs.rs#499)    /// assert_eq!(relative.as_ref().map(|s| s.as_str()), Some("../d/c.png"));
[500](https://docs.rs#500)    ///
[501](https://docs.rs#501)    /// let base = Url::parse("https://example.net/a/b.html?c=d")?;
[502](https://docs.rs#502)    /// let url = Url::parse("https://example.net/a/b.html?e=f")?;
[503](https://docs.rs#503)    /// let relative = base.make_relative(&url);
[504](https://docs.rs#504)    /// assert_eq!(relative.as_ref().map(|s| s.as_str()), Some("?e=f"));
[505](https://docs.rs#505)    /// # Ok(())
[506](https://docs.rs#506)    /// # }
[507](https://docs.rs#507)    /// # run().unwrap();
[508](https://docs.rs#508)    /// ```
[509](https://docs.rs#509)    ///
[510](https://docs.rs#510)    /// # Errors
[511](https://docs.rs#511)    ///
[512](https://docs.rs#512)    /// If this URL can't be a base for the given URL, `None` is returned.
[513](https://docs.rs#513)    /// This is for example the case if the scheme, host or port are not the same.
[514](https://docs.rs#514)    ///
[515](https://docs.rs#515)    /// [`join`]: #method.join
[516](https://docs.rs#516)    pub fn make_relative(&self, url: &Self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)> {
[517](https://docs.rs#517)        if [self](https://docs.rs#516).[cannot_be_a_base](https://docs.rs#1028-1030)() {
[518](https://docs.rs#518)            return [None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None);
[519](https://docs.rs#519)        }
[520](https://docs.rs#520)
[521](https://docs.rs#521)        // Scheme, host and port need to be the same
[522](https://docs.rs#522)        if [self](https://docs.rs#516).[scheme](https://docs.rs#903-905)() != [url](https://docs.rs#516).[scheme](https://docs.rs#903-905)() || [self](https://docs.rs#516).[host](https://docs.rs#1201-1208)() != [url](https://docs.rs#516).[host](https://docs.rs#1201-1208)() || [self](https://docs.rs#516).[port](https://docs.rs#1269-1271)() != [url](https://docs.rs#516).[port](https://docs.rs#1269-1271)() {
[523](https://docs.rs#523)            return [None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None);
[524](https://docs.rs#524)        }
[525](https://docs.rs#525)
[526](https://docs.rs#526)        // We ignore username/password at this point
[527](https://docs.rs#527)
[528](https://docs.rs#528)        // The path has to be transformed
[529](https://docs.rs#529)        let mut relative = [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)::[new](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html#method.new)();
[530](https://docs.rs#530)
[531](https://docs.rs#531)        // Extract the filename of both URIs, these need to be handled separately
[532](https://docs.rs#532)        fn extract_path_filename(s: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> (&[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html), &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) {
[533](https://docs.rs#533)            let last_slash_idx = [s](https://docs.rs#532).[rfind](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.str.html#method.rfind)('/').[unwrap_or](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#method.unwrap_or)(0);
[534](https://docs.rs#534)            let (path, filename) = [s](https://docs.rs#532).[split_at](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.str.html#method.split_at)([last_slash_idx](https://docs.rs#533));
[535](https://docs.rs#535)            if [filename](https://docs.rs#534).[is_empty](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.str.html#method.is_empty)() {
[536](https://docs.rs#536)                ([path](https://docs.rs#534), "")
[537](https://docs.rs#537)            } else {
[538](https://docs.rs#538)                ([path](https://docs.rs#534), &[filename](https://docs.rs#534)[1..])
[539](https://docs.rs#539)            }
[540](https://docs.rs#540)        }
[541](https://docs.rs#541)
[542](https://docs.rs#542)        let (base_path, base_filename) = [extract_path_filename](https://docs.rs#532-540)([self](https://docs.rs#516).[path](https://docs.rs#1391-1398)());
[543](https://docs.rs#543)        let (url_path, url_filename) = [extract_path_filename](https://docs.rs#532-540)([url](https://docs.rs#516).[path](https://docs.rs#1391-1398)());
[544](https://docs.rs#544)
[545](https://docs.rs#545)        let mut base_path = [base_path](https://docs.rs#542).[split](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.str.html#method.split)('/').[peekable](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/iterator/trait.Iterator.html#method.peekable)();
[546](https://docs.rs#546)        let mut url_path = [url_path](https://docs.rs#543).[split](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.str.html#method.split)('/').[peekable](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/iterator/trait.Iterator.html#method.peekable)();
[547](https://docs.rs#547)
[548](https://docs.rs#548)        // Skip over the common prefix
[549](https://docs.rs#549)        while base_path.peek().is_some() && base_path.peek() == url_path.peek() {
[550](https://docs.rs#550)            base_path.next();
[551](https://docs.rs#551)            url_path.next();
[552](https://docs.rs#552)        }
[553](https://docs.rs#553)
[554](https://docs.rs#554)        // Add `..` segments for the remainder of the base path
[555](https://docs.rs#555)        for base_path_segment in base_path {
[556](https://docs.rs#556)            // Skip empty last segments
[557](https://docs.rs#557)            if base_path_segment.is_empty() {
[558](https://docs.rs#558)                break;
[559](https://docs.rs#559)            }
[560](https://docs.rs#560)
[561](https://docs.rs#561)            if !relative.is_empty() {
[562](https://docs.rs#562)                relative.push('/');
[563](https://docs.rs#563)            }
[564](https://docs.rs#564)
[565](https://docs.rs#565)            relative.push_str("..");
[566](https://docs.rs#566)        }
[567](https://docs.rs#567)
[568](https://docs.rs#568)        // Append the remainder of the other URI
[569](https://docs.rs#569)        for url_path_segment in url_path {
[570](https://docs.rs#570)            if !relative.is_empty() {
[571](https://docs.rs#571)                relative.push('/');
[572](https://docs.rs#572)            }
[573](https://docs.rs#573)
[574](https://docs.rs#574)            relative.push_str(url_path_segment);
[575](https://docs.rs#575)        }
[576](https://docs.rs#576)
[577](https://docs.rs#577)        // Add the filename if they are not the same
[578](https://docs.rs#578)        if ![relative](https://docs.rs#529).[is_empty](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html#method.is_empty)() || [base_filename](https://docs.rs#542) != [url_filename](https://docs.rs#543) {
[579](https://docs.rs#579)            // If the URIs filename is empty this means that it was a directory
[580](https://docs.rs#580)            // so we'll have to append a '/'.
[581](https://docs.rs#581)            //
[582](https://docs.rs#582)            // Otherwise append it directly as the new filename.
[583](https://docs.rs#583)            if [url_filename](https://docs.rs#543).[is_empty](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.str.html#method.is_empty)() {
[584](https://docs.rs#584)                [relative](https://docs.rs#529).[push](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html#method.push)('/');
[585](https://docs.rs#585)            } else {
[586](https://docs.rs#586)                if ![relative](https://docs.rs#529).[is_empty](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html#method.is_empty)() {
[587](https://docs.rs#587)                    [relative](https://docs.rs#529).[push](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html#method.push)('/');
[588](https://docs.rs#588)                }
[589](https://docs.rs#589)                [relative](https://docs.rs#529).[push_str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html#method.push_str)([url_filename](https://docs.rs#543));
[590](https://docs.rs#590)            }
[591](https://docs.rs#591)        }
[592](https://docs.rs#592)
[593](https://docs.rs#593)        // Query and fragment are only taken from the other URI
[594](https://docs.rs#594)        if let [Some](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.Some)(query) = [url](https://docs.rs#516).[query](https://docs.rs#1471-1483)() {
[595](https://docs.rs#595)            [relative](https://docs.rs#529).[push](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html#method.push)('?');
[596](https://docs.rs#596)            [relative](https://docs.rs#529).[push_str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html#method.push_str)([query](https://docs.rs#594));
[597](https://docs.rs#597)        }
[598](https://docs.rs#598)
[599](https://docs.rs#599)        if let [Some](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.Some)(fragment) = [url](https://docs.rs#516).[fragment](https://docs.rs#1545-1550)() {
[600](https://docs.rs#600)            [relative](https://docs.rs#529).[push](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html#method.push)('#');
[601](https://docs.rs#601)            [relative](https://docs.rs#529).[push_str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html#method.push_str)([fragment](https://docs.rs#599));
[602](https://docs.rs#602)        }
[603](https://docs.rs#603)
[604](https://docs.rs#604)        [Some](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.Some)([relative](https://docs.rs#529))
[605](https://docs.rs#605)    }

[681](https://docs.rs#681)    /// For internal testing, not part of the public API.
[682](https://docs.rs#682)    ///
[683](https://docs.rs#683)    /// Methods of the `Url` struct assume a number of invariants.
[684](https://docs.rs#684)    /// This checks each of these invariants and panic if one is not met.
[685](https://docs.rs#685)    /// This is for testing rust-url itself.
[686](https://docs.rs#686)    #[doc(hidden)]
[687](https://docs.rs#687)    pub fn check_invariants(&self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<(), [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)> {
[688](https://docs.rs#688)        macro_rules! assert {
[689](https://docs.rs#689)            ($x: expr) => {
[690](https://docs.rs#690)                if !$x {
[691](https://docs.rs#691)                    return Err(format!(
[692](https://docs.rs#692)                        "!( {} ) for URL {:?}",
[693](https://docs.rs#693)                        stringify!($x),
[694](https://docs.rs#694)                        self.serialization
[695](https://docs.rs#695)                    ));
[696](https://docs.rs#696)                }
[697](https://docs.rs#697)            };
[698](https://docs.rs#698)        }
[699](https://docs.rs#699)
[700](https://docs.rs#700)        macro_rules! assert_eq {
[701](https://docs.rs#701)            ($a: expr, $b: expr) => {
[702](https://docs.rs#702)                {
[703](https://docs.rs#703)                    let a = $a;
[704](https://docs.rs#704)                    let b = $b;
[705](https://docs.rs#705)                    if a != b {
[706](https://docs.rs#706)                        return Err(format!("{:?} != {:?} ({} != {}) for URL {:?}",
[707](https://docs.rs#707)                                           a, b, stringify!($a), stringify!($b),
[708](https://docs.rs#708)                                           self.serialization))
[709](https://docs.rs#709)                    }
[710](https://docs.rs#710)                }
[711](https://docs.rs#711)            }
[712](https://docs.rs#712)        }
[713](https://docs.rs#713)
[714](https://docs.rs#714)        [assert!](https://docs.rs#688-698)(self.scheme_end >= 1);
[715](https://docs.rs#715)        [assert!](https://docs.rs#688-698)(self.byte_at(0).is_ascii_alphabetic());
[716](https://docs.rs#716)        [assert!](https://docs.rs#688-698)(self
[717](https://docs.rs#717)            .slice(1..self.scheme_end)
[718](https://docs.rs#718)            .chars()
[719](https://docs.rs#719)            .all(|c| matches!(c, 'a'..='z' | 'A'..='Z' | '0'..='9' | '+' | '-' | '.')));
[720](https://docs.rs#720)        [assert_eq!](https://docs.rs#700-712)(self.byte_at(self.scheme_end), b':');
[721](https://docs.rs#721)
[722](https://docs.rs#722)        if [self](https://docs.rs#687).[slice](https://docs.rs#2763-2768)(self.scheme_end + 1..).[starts_with](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.str.html#method.starts_with)("//") {
[723](https://docs.rs#723)            // URL with authority
[724](https://docs.rs#724)            if [self](https://docs.rs#687).username_end != [self](https://docs.rs#687).serialization.[len](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html#method.len)() as [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html) {
[725](https://docs.rs#725)                match [self](https://docs.rs#687).[byte_at](https://docs.rs#2771-2773)([self](https://docs.rs#687).username_end) {
[726](https://docs.rs#726)                    b':' => {
[727](https://docs.rs#727)                        [assert!](https://docs.rs#688-698)(self.host_start >= self.username_end + 2);
[728](https://docs.rs#728)                        [assert_eq!](https://docs.rs#700-712)(self.byte_at(self.host_start - 1), b'@');
[729](https://docs.rs#729)                    }
[730](https://docs.rs#730)                    b'@' => [assert!](https://docs.rs#688-698)(self.host_start == self.username_end + 1),
[731](https://docs.rs#731)                    _ => [assert_eq!](https://docs.rs#700-712)(self.username_end, self.scheme_end + 3),
[732](https://docs.rs#732)                }
[733](https://docs.rs#733)            }
[734](https://docs.rs#734)            [assert!](https://docs.rs#688-698)(self.host_start >= self.username_end);
[735](https://docs.rs#735)            [assert!](https://docs.rs#688-698)(self.host_end >= self.host_start);
[736](https://docs.rs#736)            let host_str = [self](https://docs.rs#687).[slice](https://docs.rs#2763-2768)(self.host_start..self.host_end);
[737](https://docs.rs#737)            match [self](https://docs.rs#687).host {
[738](https://docs.rs#738)                HostInternal::[None](https://docs.rs/host.rs.html#26) => [assert_eq!](https://docs.rs#700-712)(host_str, ""),
[739](https://docs.rs#739)                HostInternal::[Ipv4](https://docs.rs/host.rs.html#28)(address) => [assert_eq!](https://docs.rs#700-712)(host_str, address.to_string()),
[740](https://docs.rs#740)                HostInternal::[Ipv6](https://docs.rs/host.rs.html#29)(address) => {
[741](https://docs.rs#741)                    let h: [Host](https://docs.rs/host.rs.html#46-64)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)> = Host::[Ipv6](https://docs.rs/host.rs.html#63)([address](https://docs.rs#740));
[742](https://docs.rs#742)                    [assert_eq!](https://docs.rs#700-712)(host_str, h.to_string())
[743](https://docs.rs#743)                }
[744](https://docs.rs#744)                HostInternal::[Domain](https://docs.rs/host.rs.html#27) => {
[745](https://docs.rs#745)                    if [SchemeType](https://docs.rs/parser.rs.html#160-164)::[from](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.From.html#tymethod.from)([self](https://docs.rs#687).[scheme](https://docs.rs#903-905)()).[is_special](https://docs.rs/parser.rs.html#167-169)() {
[746](https://docs.rs#746)                        [assert!](https://docs.rs#688-698)(!host_str.is_empty())
[747](https://docs.rs#747)                    }
[748](https://docs.rs#748)                }
[749](https://docs.rs#749)            }
[750](https://docs.rs#750)            if [self](https://docs.rs#687).path_start == [self](https://docs.rs#687).host_end {
[751](https://docs.rs#751)                [assert_eq!](https://docs.rs#700-712)(self.port, None);
[752](https://docs.rs#752)            } else {
[753](https://docs.rs#753)                [assert_eq!](https://docs.rs#700-712)(self.byte_at(self.host_end), b':');
[754](https://docs.rs#754)                let port_str = [self](https://docs.rs#687).[slice](https://docs.rs#2763-2768)(self.host_end + 1..self.path_start);
[755](https://docs.rs#755)                [assert_eq!](https://docs.rs#700-712)(
[756](https://docs.rs#756)                    self.port,
[757](https://docs.rs#757)                    Some(port_str.parse::<u16>().expect("Couldn't parse port?"))
[758](https://docs.rs#758)                );
[759](https://docs.rs#759)            }
[760](https://docs.rs#760)            [assert!](https://docs.rs#688-698)(
[761](https://docs.rs#761)                self.path_start as usize == self.serialization.len()
[762](https://docs.rs#762)                    || matches!(self.byte_at(self.path_start), b'/' | b'#' | b'?')
[763](https://docs.rs#763)            );
[764](https://docs.rs#764)        } else {
[765](https://docs.rs#765)            // Anarchist URL (no authority)
[766](https://docs.rs#766)            [assert_eq!](https://docs.rs#700-712)(self.username_end, self.scheme_end + 1);
[767](https://docs.rs#767)            [assert_eq!](https://docs.rs#700-712)(self.host_start, self.scheme_end + 1);
[768](https://docs.rs#768)            [assert_eq!](https://docs.rs#700-712)(self.host_end, self.scheme_end + 1);
[769](https://docs.rs#769)            [assert_eq!](https://docs.rs#700-712)(self.host, HostInternal::None);
[770](https://docs.rs#770)            [assert_eq!](https://docs.rs#700-712)(self.port, None);
[771](https://docs.rs#771)            if [self](https://docs.rs#687).[path](https://docs.rs#1391-1398)().[starts_with](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.str.html#method.starts_with)("//") {
[772](https://docs.rs#772)                // special case when first path segment is empty
[773](https://docs.rs#773)                [assert_eq!](https://docs.rs#700-712)(self.byte_at(self.scheme_end + 1), b'/');
[774](https://docs.rs#774)                [assert_eq!](https://docs.rs#700-712)(self.byte_at(self.scheme_end + 2), b'.');
[775](https://docs.rs#775)                [assert_eq!](https://docs.rs#700-712)(self.path_start, self.scheme_end + 3);
[776](https://docs.rs#776)            } else {
[777](https://docs.rs#777)                [assert_eq!](https://docs.rs#700-712)(self.path_start, self.scheme_end + 1);
[778](https://docs.rs#778)            }
[779](https://docs.rs#779)        }
[780](https://docs.rs#780)        if let [Some](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.Some)(start) = [self](https://docs.rs#687).query_start {
[781](https://docs.rs#781)            [assert!](https://docs.rs#688-698)(start >= self.path_start);
[782](https://docs.rs#782)            [assert_eq!](https://docs.rs#700-712)(self.byte_at(start), b'?');
[783](https://docs.rs#783)        }
[784](https://docs.rs#784)        if let [Some](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.Some)(start) = [self](https://docs.rs#687).fragment_start {
[785](https://docs.rs#785)            [assert!](https://docs.rs#688-698)(start >= self.path_start);
[786](https://docs.rs#786)            [assert_eq!](https://docs.rs#700-712)(self.byte_at(start), b'#');
[787](https://docs.rs#787)        }
[788](https://docs.rs#788)        if let ([Some](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.Some)(query_start), [Some](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.Some)(fragment_start)) = ([self](https://docs.rs#687).query_start, [self](https://docs.rs#687).fragment_start) {
[789](https://docs.rs#789)            [assert!](https://docs.rs#688-698)(fragment_start > query_start);
[790](https://docs.rs#790)        }
[791](https://docs.rs#791)
[792](https://docs.rs#792)        let other = Self::[parse](https://docs.rs#341-343)([self](https://docs.rs#687).[as_str](https://docs.rs#653-655)()).[expect](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html#method.expect)("Failed to parse myself?");
[793](https://docs.rs#793)        [assert_eq!](https://docs.rs#700-712)(&self.serialization, &other.serialization);
[794](https://docs.rs#794)        [assert_eq!](https://docs.rs#700-712)(self.scheme_end, other.scheme_end);
[795](https://docs.rs#795)        [assert_eq!](https://docs.rs#700-712)(self.username_end, other.username_end);
[796](https://docs.rs#796)        [assert_eq!](https://docs.rs#700-712)(self.host_start, other.host_start);
[797](https://docs.rs#797)        [assert_eq!](https://docs.rs#700-712)(self.host_end, other.host_end);
[798](https://docs.rs#798)        [assert!](https://docs.rs#688-698)(
[799](https://docs.rs#799)            self.host == other.host ||
[800](https://docs.rs#800)                // XXX No host round-trips to empty host.
[801](https://docs.rs#801)                // See https://github.com/whatwg/url/issues/79
[802](https://docs.rs#802)                (self.host_str(), other.host_str()) == (None, Some(""))
[803](https://docs.rs#803)        );
[804](https://docs.rs#804)        [assert_eq!](https://docs.rs#700-712)(self.port, other.port);
[805](https://docs.rs#805)        [assert_eq!](https://docs.rs#700-712)(self.path_start, other.path_start);
[806](https://docs.rs#806)        [assert_eq!](https://docs.rs#700-712)(self.query_start, other.query_start);
[807](https://docs.rs#807)        [assert_eq!](https://docs.rs#700-712)(self.fragment_start, other.fragment_start);
[808](https://docs.rs#808)        [Ok](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html#variant.Ok)(())
[809](https://docs.rs#809)    }

[811](https://docs.rs#811)    /// Return the origin of this URL (<https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#origin>)

[928](https://docs.rs#928)    /// Return whether the URL has an 'authority',

[933](https://docs.rs#933)    ///

[951](https://docs.rs#951)    /// # Ok(())

[961](https://docs.rs#961)    /// Return the authority of this URL as an ASCII string.
[962](https://docs.rs#962)    ///
[963](https://docs.rs#963)    /// Non-ASCII domains are punycode-encoded per IDNA if this is the host
[964](https://docs.rs#964)    /// of a special URL, or percent encoded for non-special URLs.
[965](https://docs.rs#965)    /// IPv6 addresses are given between `[` and `]` brackets.
[966](https://docs.rs#966)    /// Ports are omitted if they match the well known port of a special URL.
[967](https://docs.rs#967)    ///
[968](https://docs.rs#968)    /// Username and password are percent-encoded.
[969](https://docs.rs#969)    ///
[970](https://docs.rs#970)    /// See also the `has_authority` method.
[971](https://docs.rs#971)    ///
[972](https://docs.rs#972)    /// # Examples
[973](https://docs.rs#973)    ///
[974](https://docs.rs#974)    /// ```
[975](https://docs.rs#975)    /// use url::Url;
[976](https://docs.rs#976)    /// # use url::ParseError;
[977](https://docs.rs#977)    ///
[978](https://docs.rs#978)    /// # fn run() -> Result<(), ParseError> {
[979](https://docs.rs#979)    /// let url = Url::parse("unix:/run/foo.socket")?;
[980](https://docs.rs#980)    /// assert_eq!(url.authority(), "");
[981](https://docs.rs#981)    /// let url = Url::parse("file:///tmp/foo")?;
[982](https://docs.rs#982)    /// assert_eq!(url.authority(), "");
[983](https://docs.rs#983)    /// let url = Url::parse("https://user:password@example.com/tmp/foo")?;
[984](https://docs.rs#984)    /// assert_eq!(url.authority(), "user:password@example.com");
[985](https://docs.rs#985)    /// let url = Url::parse("irc://àlex.рф.example.com:6667/foo")?;
[986](https://docs.rs#986)    /// assert_eq!(url.authority(), "%C3%A0lex.%D1%80%D1%84.example.com:6667");
[987](https://docs.rs#987)    /// let url = Url::parse("http://àlex.рф.example.com:80/foo")?;
[988](https://docs.rs#988)    /// assert_eq!(url.authority(), "xn--lex-8ka.xn--p1ai.example.com");
[989](https://docs.rs#989)    /// # Ok(())
[990](https://docs.rs#990)    /// # }
[991](https://docs.rs#991)    /// # run().unwrap();
[992](https://docs.rs#992)    /// ```
[993](https://docs.rs#993)    pub fn authority(&self) -> &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html) {
[994](https://docs.rs#994)        let scheme_separator_len = "://".[len](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.str.html#method.len)() as [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html);
[995](https://docs.rs#995)        if [self](https://docs.rs#993).[has_authority](https://docs.rs#956-959)() && [self](https://docs.rs#993).path_start > [self](https://docs.rs#993).scheme_end + [scheme_separator_len](https://docs.rs#994) {
[996](https://docs.rs#996)            [self](https://docs.rs#993).[slice](https://docs.rs#2763-2768)(self.scheme_end + scheme_separator_len..self.path_start)
[997](https://docs.rs#997)        } else {
[998](https://docs.rs#998)            ""
[999](https://docs.rs#999)        }
[1000](https://docs.rs#1000)    }

[1308](https://docs.rs#1308)    /// `default_port_number` provides an opportunity to provide the actual port number.
[1309](https://docs.rs#1309)    /// In non-example code this should be implemented either simply as `|| None`,
[1310](https://docs.rs#1310)    /// or by matching on the URL’s `.scheme()`.
[1311](https://docs.rs#1311)    ///
[1312](https://docs.rs#1312)    /// If the host is a domain, it is resolved using the standard library’s DNS support.
[1313](https://docs.rs#1313)    ///
[1314](https://docs.rs#1314)    /// # Examples
[1315](https://docs.rs#1315)    ///
[1316](https://docs.rs#1316)    /// ```no_run
[1317](https://docs.rs#1317)    /// let url = url::Url::parse("https://example.net/").unwrap();
[1318](https://docs.rs#1318)    /// let addrs = url.socket_addrs(|| None).unwrap();
[1319](https://docs.rs#1319)    /// std::net::TcpStream::connect(&*addrs)
[1320](https://docs.rs#1320)    /// # ;
[1321](https://docs.rs#1321)    /// ```
[1322](https://docs.rs#1322)    ///
[1323](https://docs.rs#1323)    /// ```
[1324](https://docs.rs#1324)    /// /// With application-specific known default port numbers
[1325](https://docs.rs#1325)    /// fn socket_addrs(url: url::Url) -> std::io::Result<Vec<std::net::SocketAddr>> {
[1326](https://docs.rs#1326)    ///     url.socket_addrs(|| match url.scheme() {
[1327](https://docs.rs#1327)    ///         "socks5" | "socks5h" => Some(1080),
[1328](https://docs.rs#1328)    ///         _ => None,
[1329](https://docs.rs#1329)    ///     })
[1330](https://docs.rs#1330)    /// }
[1331](https://docs.rs#1331)    /// ```
[1332](https://docs.rs#1332)    #[cfg(feature = "std")]
[1333](https://docs.rs#1333)    #[cfg(any(
[1334](https://docs.rs#1334)        unix,
[1335](https://docs.rs#1335)        windows,
[1336](https://docs.rs#1336)        target_os = "redox",
[1337](https://docs.rs#1337)        target_os = "wasi",
[1338](https://docs.rs#1338)        target_os = "hermit"
[1339](https://docs.rs#1339)    ))]
[1340](https://docs.rs#1340)    pub fn socket_addrs(
[1341](https://docs.rs#1341)        &self,
[1342](https://docs.rs#1342)        default_port_number: impl [Fn](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/function/trait.Fn.html)() -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[u16](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u16.html)>,
[1343](https://docs.rs#1343)    ) -> io::[Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/error/type.Result.html)<alloc::vec::[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[SocketAddr](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/net/socket_addr/enum.SocketAddr.html)>> {
[1344](https://docs.rs#1344)        // Note: trying to avoid the Vec allocation by returning `impl AsRef<[SocketAddr]>`
[1345](https://docs.rs#1345)        // causes borrowck issues because the return value borrows `default_port_number`:
[1346](https://docs.rs#1346)        //
[1347](https://docs.rs#1347)        // https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/blob/master/text/1951-expand-impl-trait.md#scoping-for-type-and-lifetime-parameters
[1348](https://docs.rs#1348)        //
[1349](https://docs.rs#1349)        // > This RFC proposes that *all* type parameters are considered in scope
[1350](https://docs.rs#1350)        // > for `impl Trait` in return position
[1351](https://docs.rs#1351)
[1352](https://docs.rs#1352)        fn io_result<T>(opt: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<T>, message: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> io::[Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/error/type.Result.html)<T> {
[1353](https://docs.rs#1353)            [opt](https://docs.rs#1352).[ok_or_else](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#method.ok_or_else)(|| io::[Error](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/error/struct.Error.html)::[new](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/error/struct.Error.html#method.new)(io::ErrorKind::[InvalidData](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/io/error/enum.ErrorKind.html#variant.InvalidData), [message](https://docs.rs#1352)))
[1354](https://docs.rs#1354)        }
[1355](https://docs.rs#1355)
[1356](https://docs.rs#1356)        let host = io_result(self.host(), "No host name in the URL")?;
[1357](https://docs.rs#1357)        let port = io_result(
[1358](https://docs.rs#1358)            self.port_or_known_default().or_else(default_port_number),
[1359](https://docs.rs#1359)            "No port number in the URL",
[1360](https://docs.rs#1360)        )?;
[1361](https://docs.rs#1361)        [Ok](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html#variant.Ok)(match [host](https://docs.rs#1356) {
[1362](https://docs.rs#1362)            Host::[Domain](https://docs.rs/host.rs.html#51)(domain) => (domain, port).to_socket_addrs()?.[collect](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/iterator/trait.Iterator.html#method.collect)(),
[1363](https://docs.rs#1363)            Host::[Ipv4](https://docs.rs/host.rs.html#56)(ip) => [vec!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/macro.vec.html)[(ip, port).into()],
[1364](https://docs.rs#1364)            Host::[Ipv6](https://docs.rs/host.rs.html#63)(ip) => [vec!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/macro.vec.html)[(ip, port).into()],
[1365](https://docs.rs#1365)        })

[1368](https://docs.rs#1368)    /// Return the path for this URL, as a percent-encoded ASCII string.
[1369](https://docs.rs#1369)    /// For cannot-be-a-base URLs, this is an arbitrary string that doesn’t start with '/'.
[1370](https://docs.rs#1370)    /// For other URLs, this starts with a '/' slash
[1371](https://docs.rs#1371)    /// and continues with slash-separated path segments.
[1372](https://docs.rs#1372)    ///
[1373](https://docs.rs#1373)    /// # Examples
[1374](https://docs.rs#1374)    ///
[1375](https://docs.rs#1375)    /// ```rust
[1376](https://docs.rs#1376)    /// use url::{Url, ParseError};
[1377](https://docs.rs#1377)    ///
[1378](https://docs.rs#1378)    /// # fn run() -> Result<(), ParseError> {
[1379](https://docs.rs#1379)    /// let url = Url::parse("https://example.com/api/versions?page=2")?;
[1380](https://docs.rs#1380)    /// assert_eq!(url.path(), "/api/versions");
[1381](https://docs.rs#1381)    ///
[1382](https://docs.rs#1382)    /// let url = Url::parse("https://example.com")?;
[1383](https://docs.rs#1383)    /// assert_eq!(url.path(), "/");
[1384](https://docs.rs#1384)    ///
[1385](https://docs.rs#1385)    /// let url = Url::parse("https://example.com/countries/việt nam")?;
[1386](https://docs.rs#1386)    /// assert_eq!(url.path(), "/countries/vi%E1%BB%87t%20nam");
[1387](https://docs.rs#1387)    /// # Ok(())
[1388](https://docs.rs#1388)    /// # }
[1389](https://docs.rs#1389)    /// # run().unwrap();
[1390](https://docs.rs#1390)    /// ```
[1391](https://docs.rs#1391)    pub fn path(&self) -> &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html) {
[1392](https://docs.rs#1392)        match ([self](https://docs.rs#1391).query_start, [self](https://docs.rs#1391).fragment_start) {
[1393](https://docs.rs#1393)            ([None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None), [None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None)) => [self](https://docs.rs#1391).[slice](https://docs.rs#2763-2768)(self.path_start..),
[1394](https://docs.rs#1394)            ([Some](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.Some)(next_component_start), _) | ([None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None), [Some](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.Some)(next_component_start)) => {
[1395](https://docs.rs#1395)                [self](https://docs.rs#1391).[slice](https://docs.rs#2763-2768)(self.path_start..next_component_start)
[1396](https://docs.rs#1396)            }
[1397](https://docs.rs#1397)        }
[1398](https://docs.rs#1398)    }
[1399](https://docs.rs#1399)
[1400](https://docs.rs#1400)    /// Unless this URL is cannot-be-a-base,
[1401](https://docs.rs#1401)    /// return an iterator of '/' slash-separated path segments,
[1402](https://docs.rs#1402)    /// each as a percent-encoded ASCII string.
[1403](https://docs.rs#1403)    ///
[1404](https://docs.rs#1404)    /// Return `None` for cannot-be-a-base URLs.
[1405](https://docs.rs#1405)    ///
[1406](https://docs.rs#1406)    /// When `Some` is returned, the iterator always contains at least one string
[1407](https://docs.rs#1407)    /// (which may be empty).
[1408](https://docs.rs#1408)    ///
[1409](https://docs.rs#1409)    /// # Examples
[1410](https://docs.rs#1410)    ///
[1411](https://docs.rs#1411)    /// ```
[1412](https://docs.rs#1412)    /// use url::Url;
[1413](https://docs.rs#1413)    ///
[1414](https://docs.rs#1414)    /// # #[cfg(feature = "std")]
[1415](https://docs.rs#1415)    /// # use std::error::Error;
[1416](https://docs.rs#1416)    /// # #[cfg(not(feature = "std"))]
[1417](https://docs.rs#1417)    /// # use core::error::Error;
[1418](https://docs.rs#1418)    ///
[1419](https://docs.rs#1419)    /// # fn run() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> {
[1420](https://docs.rs#1420)    /// let url = Url::parse("https://example.com/foo/bar")?;
[1421](https://docs.rs#1421)    /// let mut path_segments = url.path_segments().ok_or_else(|| "cannot be base")?;
[1422](https://docs.rs#1422)    /// assert_eq!(path_segments.next(), Some("foo"));
[1423](https://docs.rs#1423)    /// assert_eq!(path_segments.next(), Some("bar"));
[1424](https://docs.rs#1424)    /// assert_eq!(path_segments.next(), None);
[1425](https://docs.rs#1425)    ///
[1426](https://docs.rs#1426)    /// let url = Url::parse("https://example.com")?;
[1427](https://docs.rs#1427)    /// let mut path_segments = url.path_segments().ok_or_else(|| "cannot be base")?;
[1428](https://docs.rs#1428)    /// assert_eq!(path_segments.next(), Some(""));
[1429](https://docs.rs#1429)    /// assert_eq!(path_segments.next(), None);
[1430](https://docs.rs#1430)    ///
[1431](https://docs.rs#1431)    /// let url = Url::parse("data:text/plain,HelloWorld")?;
[1432](https://docs.rs#1432)    /// assert!(url.path_segments().is_none());
[1433](https://docs.rs#1433)    ///
[1434](https://docs.rs#1434)    /// let url = Url::parse("https://example.com/countries/việt nam")?;
[1435](https://docs.rs#1435)    /// let mut path_segments = url.path_segments().ok_or_else(|| "cannot be base")?;
[1436](https://docs.rs#1436)    /// assert_eq!(path_segments.next(), Some("countries"));
[1437](https://docs.rs#1437)    /// assert_eq!(path_segments.next(), Some("vi%E1%BB%87t%20nam"));
[1438](https://docs.rs#1438)    /// # Ok(())
[1439](https://docs.rs#1439)    /// # }
[1440](https://docs.rs#1440)    /// # run().unwrap();
[1441](https://docs.rs#1441)    /// ```
[1442](https://docs.rs#1442)    pub fn path_segments(&self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<str::[Split](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/str/iter/struct.Split.html)<'_, [char](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.char.html)>> {
[1443](https://docs.rs#1443)        let path = [self](https://docs.rs#1442).[path](https://docs.rs#1391-1398)();
[1444](https://docs.rs#1444)        [path](https://docs.rs#1443).[strip_prefix](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.str.html#method.strip_prefix)('/').[map](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#method.map)(|remainder| [remainder](https://docs.rs#1444).[split](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.str.html#method.split)('/'))

[1513](https://docs.rs#1513)    /// Return this URL’s fragment identifier, if any.
[1514](https://docs.rs#1514)    ///
[1515](https://docs.rs#1515)    /// A fragment is the part of the URL after the `#` symbol.
[1516](https://docs.rs#1516)    /// The fragment is optional and, if present, contains a fragment identifier
[1517](https://docs.rs#1517)    /// that identifies a secondary resource, such as a section heading
[1518](https://docs.rs#1518)    /// of a document.
[1519](https://docs.rs#1519)    ///
[1520](https://docs.rs#1520)    /// In HTML, the fragment identifier is usually the id attribute of a an element
[1521](https://docs.rs#1521)    /// that is scrolled to on load. Browsers typically will not send the fragment portion
[1522](https://docs.rs#1522)    /// of a URL to the server.
[1523](https://docs.rs#1523)    ///
[1524](https://docs.rs#1524)    /// **Note:** the parser did *not* percent-encode this component,
[1525](https://docs.rs#1525)    /// but the input may have been percent-encoded already.
[1526](https://docs.rs#1526)    ///
[1527](https://docs.rs#1527)    /// # Examples
[1528](https://docs.rs#1528)    ///
[1529](https://docs.rs#1529)    /// ```rust
[1530](https://docs.rs#1530)    /// use url::Url;
[1531](https://docs.rs#1531)    /// # use url::ParseError;
[1532](https://docs.rs#1532)    ///
[1533](https://docs.rs#1533)    /// # fn run() -> Result<(), ParseError> {
[1534](https://docs.rs#1534)    /// let url = Url::parse("https://example.com/data.csv#row=4")?;
[1535](https://docs.rs#1535)    ///
[1536](https://docs.rs#1536)    /// assert_eq!(url.fragment(), Some("row=4"));
[1537](https://docs.rs#1537)    ///
[1538](https://docs.rs#1538)    /// let url = Url::parse("https://example.com/data.csv#cell=4,1-6,2")?;
[1539](https://docs.rs#1539)    ///
[1540](https://docs.rs#1540)    /// assert_eq!(url.fragment(), Some("cell=4,1-6,2"));
[1541](https://docs.rs#1541)    /// # Ok(())
[1542](https://docs.rs#1542)    /// # }
[1543](https://docs.rs#1543)    /// # run().unwrap();
[1544](https://docs.rs#1544)    /// ```
[1545](https://docs.rs#1545)    pub fn fragment(&self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)> {
[1546](https://docs.rs#1546)        [self](https://docs.rs#1545).fragment_start.[map](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#method.map)(|start| {
[1547](https://docs.rs#1547)            [debug_assert!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/macro.debug_assert.html)(self.byte_at(start) == b'#');
[1548](https://docs.rs#1548)            [self](https://docs.rs#1545).[slice](https://docs.rs#2763-2768)(start + 1..)
[1549](https://docs.rs#1549)        })
[1550](https://docs.rs#1550)    }
[1551](https://docs.rs#1551)
[1552](https://docs.rs#1552)    fn mutate<F: [FnOnce](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/function/trait.FnOnce.html)(&mut [Parser](https://docs.rs/parser.rs.html#338-344)<'_>) -> R, R>(&mut self, f: F) -> R {
[1553](https://docs.rs#1553)        let mut parser = [Parser](https://docs.rs/parser.rs.html#338-344)::[for_setter](https://docs.rs/parser.rs.html#368-376)(mem::[take](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/mem/fn.take.html)(&mut [self](https://docs.rs#1552).serialization));

[1669](https://docs.rs#1669)    /// Manipulate this URL’s query string, viewed as a sequence of name/value pairs
[1670](https://docs.rs#1670)    /// in `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` syntax.
[1671](https://docs.rs#1671)    ///
[1672](https://docs.rs#1672)    /// The return value has a method-chaining API:
[1673](https://docs.rs#1673)    ///
[1674](https://docs.rs#1674)    /// ```rust
[1675](https://docs.rs#1675)    /// # use url::{Url, ParseError};
[1676](https://docs.rs#1676)    ///
[1677](https://docs.rs#1677)    /// # fn run() -> Result<(), ParseError> {
[1678](https://docs.rs#1678)    /// let mut url = Url::parse("https://example.net?lang=fr#nav")?;
[1679](https://docs.rs#1679)    /// assert_eq!(url.query(), Some("lang=fr"));
[1680](https://docs.rs#1680)    ///
[1681](https://docs.rs#1681)    /// url.query_pairs_mut().append_pair("foo", "bar");
[1682](https://docs.rs#1682)    /// assert_eq!(url.query(), Some("lang=fr&foo=bar"));
[1683](https://docs.rs#1683)    /// assert_eq!(url.as_str(), "https://example.net/?lang=fr&foo=bar#nav");
[1684](https://docs.rs#1684)    ///
[1685](https://docs.rs#1685)    /// url.query_pairs_mut()
[1686](https://docs.rs#1686)    ///     .clear()
[1687](https://docs.rs#1687)    ///     .append_pair("foo", "bar & baz")
[1688](https://docs.rs#1688)    ///     .append_pair("saisons", "\u{00C9}t\u{00E9}+hiver");
[1689](https://docs.rs#1689)    /// assert_eq!(url.query(), Some("foo=bar+%26+baz&saisons=%C3%89t%C3%A9%2Bhiver"));
[1690](https://docs.rs#1690)    /// assert_eq!(url.as_str(),
[1691](https://docs.rs#1691)    ///            "https://example.net/?foo=bar+%26+baz&saisons=%C3%89t%C3%A9%2Bhiver#nav");
[1692](https://docs.rs#1692)    /// # Ok(())
[1693](https://docs.rs#1693)    /// # }
[1694](https://docs.rs#1694)    /// # run().unwrap();
[1695](https://docs.rs#1695)    /// ```
[1696](https://docs.rs#1696)    ///
[1697](https://docs.rs#1697)    /// Note: `url.query_pairs_mut().clear();` is equivalent to `url.set_query(Some(""))`,
[1698](https://docs.rs#1698)    /// not `url.set_query(None)`.

[1819](https://docs.rs#1819)    /// Change this URL’s port number.
[1820](https://docs.rs#1820)    ///
[1821](https://docs.rs#1821)    /// Note that default port numbers are not reflected in the serialization.
[1822](https://docs.rs#1822)    ///
[1823](https://docs.rs#1823)    /// If this URL is cannot-be-a-base, does not have a host, or has the `file` scheme;
[1824](https://docs.rs#1824)    /// do nothing and return `Err`.
[1825](https://docs.rs#1825)    ///
[1826](https://docs.rs#1826)    /// # Examples
[1827](https://docs.rs#1827)    ///
[1828](https://docs.rs#1828)    /// ```
[1829](https://docs.rs#1829)    /// use url::Url;
[1830](https://docs.rs#1830)    ///
[1831](https://docs.rs#1831)    /// # #[cfg(feature = "std")]
[1832](https://docs.rs#1832)    /// # use std::error::Error;
[1833](https://docs.rs#1833)    /// # #[cfg(not(feature = "std"))]
[1834](https://docs.rs#1834)    /// # use core::error::Error;
[1835](https://docs.rs#1835)    ///
[1836](https://docs.rs#1836)    /// # fn run() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> {
[1837](https://docs.rs#1837)    /// let mut url = Url::parse("ssh://example.net:2048/")?;
[1838](https://docs.rs#1838)    ///
[1839](https://docs.rs#1839)    /// url.set_port(Some(4096)).map_err(|_| "cannot be base")?;
[1840](https://docs.rs#1840)    /// assert_eq!(url.as_str(), "ssh://example.net:4096/");
[1841](https://docs.rs#1841)    ///
[1842](https://docs.rs#1842)    /// url.set_port(None).map_err(|_| "cannot be base")?;
[1843](https://docs.rs#1843)    /// assert_eq!(url.as_str(), "ssh://example.net/");
[1844](https://docs.rs#1844)    /// # Ok(())
[1845](https://docs.rs#1845)    /// # }
[1846](https://docs.rs#1846)    /// # run().unwrap();
[1847](https://docs.rs#1847)    /// ```
[1848](https://docs.rs#1848)    ///
[1849](https://docs.rs#1849)    /// Known default port numbers are not reflected:
[1850](https://docs.rs#1850)    ///
[1851](https://docs.rs#1851)    /// ```rust
[1852](https://docs.rs#1852)    /// use url::Url;
[1853](https://docs.rs#1853)    ///
[1854](https://docs.rs#1854)    /// # #[cfg(feature = "std")]
[1855](https://docs.rs#1855)    /// # use std::error::Error;
[1856](https://docs.rs#1856)    /// # #[cfg(not(feature = "std"))]
[1857](https://docs.rs#1857)    /// # use core::error::Error;
[1858](https://docs.rs#1858)    ///
[1859](https://docs.rs#1859)    /// # fn run() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> {
[1860](https://docs.rs#1860)    /// let mut url = Url::parse("https://example.org/")?;
[1861](https://docs.rs#1861)    ///
[1862](https://docs.rs#1862)    /// url.set_port(Some(443)).map_err(|_| "cannot be base")?;
[1863](https://docs.rs#1863)    /// assert!(url.port().is_none());
[1864](https://docs.rs#1864)    /// # Ok(())
[1865](https://docs.rs#1865)    /// # }

[1883](https://docs.rs#1883)    /// # Ok(())

[1939](https://docs.rs#1939)    /// Change this URL’s host.
[1940](https://docs.rs#1940)    ///
[1941](https://docs.rs#1941)    /// Removing the host (calling this with `None`)
[1942](https://docs.rs#1942)    /// will also remove any username, password, and port number.
[1943](https://docs.rs#1943)    ///
[1944](https://docs.rs#1944)    /// # Examples
[1945](https://docs.rs#1945)    ///
[1946](https://docs.rs#1946)    /// Change host:
[1947](https://docs.rs#1947)    ///
[1948](https://docs.rs#1948)    /// ```
[1949](https://docs.rs#1949)    /// use url::Url;
[1950](https://docs.rs#1950)    /// # use url::ParseError;
[1951](https://docs.rs#1951)    ///
[1952](https://docs.rs#1952)    /// # fn run() -> Result<(), ParseError> {
[1953](https://docs.rs#1953)    /// let mut url = Url::parse("https://example.net")?;
[1954](https://docs.rs#1954)    /// let result = url.set_host(Some("rust-lang.org"));
[1955](https://docs.rs#1955)    /// assert!(result.is_ok());
[1956](https://docs.rs#1956)    /// assert_eq!(url.as_str(), "https://rust-lang.org/");
[1957](https://docs.rs#1957)    /// # Ok(())
[1958](https://docs.rs#1958)    /// # }
[1959](https://docs.rs#1959)    /// # run().unwrap();
[1960](https://docs.rs#1960)    /// ```
[1961](https://docs.rs#1961)    ///
[1962](https://docs.rs#1962)    /// Remove host:
[1963](https://docs.rs#1963)    ///
[1964](https://docs.rs#1964)    /// ```
[1965](https://docs.rs#1965)    /// use url::Url;
[1966](https://docs.rs#1966)    /// # use url::ParseError;
[1967](https://docs.rs#1967)    ///
[1968](https://docs.rs#1968)    /// # fn run() -> Result<(), ParseError> {
[1969](https://docs.rs#1969)    /// let mut url = Url::parse("foo://example.net")?;
[1970](https://docs.rs#1970)    /// let result = url.set_host(None);
[1971](https://docs.rs#1971)    /// assert!(result.is_ok());
[1972](https://docs.rs#1972)    /// assert_eq!(url.as_str(), "foo:/");
[1973](https://docs.rs#1973)    /// # Ok(())
[1974](https://docs.rs#1974)    /// # }
[1975](https://docs.rs#1975)    /// # run().unwrap();
[1976](https://docs.rs#1976)    /// ```
[1977](https://docs.rs#1977)    ///
[1978](https://docs.rs#1978)    /// Cannot remove host for 'special' schemes (e.g. `http`):
[1979](https://docs.rs#1979)    ///
[1980](https://docs.rs#1980)    /// ```
[1981](https://docs.rs#1981)    /// use url::Url;
[1982](https://docs.rs#1982)    /// # use url::ParseError;

[2351](https://docs.rs#2351)    /// Change this URL’s scheme.
[2352](https://docs.rs#2352)    ///
[2353](https://docs.rs#2353)    /// Do nothing and return `Err` under the following circumstances:
[2354](https://docs.rs#2354)    ///
[2355](https://docs.rs#2355)    /// * If the new scheme is not in `[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9+.-]+`
[2356](https://docs.rs#2356)    /// * If this URL is cannot-be-a-base and the new scheme is one of
[2357](https://docs.rs#2357)    ///   `http`, `https`, `ws`, `wss` or `ftp`
[2358](https://docs.rs#2358)    /// * If either the old or new scheme is `http`, `https`, `ws`,
[2359](https://docs.rs#2359)    ///   `wss` or `ftp` and the other is not one of these
[2360](https://docs.rs#2360)    /// * If the new scheme is `file` and this URL includes credentials
[2361](https://docs.rs#2361)    ///   or has a non-null port
[2362](https://docs.rs#2362)    /// * If this URL's scheme is `file` and its host is empty or null
[2363](https://docs.rs#2363)    ///
[2364](https://docs.rs#2364)    /// See also [the URL specification's section on legal scheme state
[2365](https://docs.rs#2365)    /// overrides](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#scheme-state).
[2366](https://docs.rs#2366)    ///
[2367](https://docs.rs#2367)    /// # Examples
[2368](https://docs.rs#2368)    ///
[2369](https://docs.rs#2369)    /// Change the URL’s scheme from `https` to `http`:
[2370](https://docs.rs#2370)    ///
[2371](https://docs.rs#2371)    /// ```
[2372](https://docs.rs#2372)    /// use url::Url;
[2373](https://docs.rs#2373)    /// # use url::ParseError;
[2374](https://docs.rs#2374)    ///
[2375](https://docs.rs#2375)    /// # fn run() -> Result<(), ParseError> {
[2376](https://docs.rs#2376)    /// let mut url = Url::parse("https://example.net")?;
[2377](https://docs.rs#2377)    /// let result = url.set_scheme("http");
[2378](https://docs.rs#2378)    /// assert_eq!(url.as_str(), "http://example.net/");
[2379](https://docs.rs#2379)    /// assert!(result.is_ok());
[2380](https://docs.rs#2380)    /// # Ok(())
[2381](https://docs.rs#2381)    /// # }
[2382](https://docs.rs#2382)    /// # run().unwrap();
[2383](https://docs.rs#2383)    /// ```
[2384](https://docs.rs#2384)    /// Change the URL’s scheme from `foo` to `bar`:
[2385](https://docs.rs#2385)    ///
[2386](https://docs.rs#2386)    /// ```
[2387](https://docs.rs#2387)    /// use url::Url;
[2388](https://docs.rs#2388)    /// # use url::ParseError;
[2389](https://docs.rs#2389)    ///
[2390](https://docs.rs#2390)    /// # fn run() -> Result<(), ParseError> {
[2391](https://docs.rs#2391)    /// let mut url = Url::parse("foo://example.net")?;
[2392](https://docs.rs#2392)    /// let result = url.set_scheme("bar");
[2393](https://docs.rs#2393)    /// assert_eq!(url.as_str(), "bar://example.net");
[2394](https://docs.rs#2394)    /// assert!(result.is_ok());
[2395](https://docs.rs#2395)    /// # Ok(())
[2396](https://docs.rs#2396)    /// # }
[2397](https://docs.rs#2397)    /// # run().unwrap();
[2398](https://docs.rs#2398)    /// ```
[2399](https://docs.rs#2399)    ///
[2400](https://docs.rs#2400)    /// Cannot change URL’s scheme from `https` to `foõ`:

[2571](https://docs.rs#2571)    /// Convert a directory name as `std::path::Path` into an URL in the `file` scheme.
[2572](https://docs.rs#2572)    ///
[2573](https://docs.rs#2573)    /// This returns `Err` if the given path is not absolute or,
[2574](https://docs.rs#2574)    /// on Windows, if the prefix is not a disk prefix (e.g. `C:`) or a UNC prefix (`\\`).
[2575](https://docs.rs#2575)    ///
[2576](https://docs.rs#2576)    /// Compared to `from_file_path`, this ensure that URL’s the path has a trailing slash
[2577](https://docs.rs#2577)    /// so that the entire path is considered when using this URL as a base URL.

[2579](https://docs.rs#2579)    /// For example:
[2580](https://docs.rs#2580)    ///

[2582](https://docs.rs#2582)    ///   as the base URL is `file:///var/www/index.html`
[2583](https://docs.rs#2583)    /// * `"index.html"` parsed with `Url::from_file_path(Path::new("/var/www"))`
[2584](https://docs.rs#2584)    ///   as the base URL is `file:///var/index.html`, which might not be what was intended.
[2585](https://docs.rs#2585)    ///
[2586](https://docs.rs#2586)    /// Note that `std::path` does not consider trailing slashes significant
[2587](https://docs.rs#2587)    /// and usually does not include them (e.g. in `Path::parent()`).

[2589](https://docs.rs#2589)    /// This method is only available if the `std` Cargo feature is enabled.
[2590](https://docs.rs#2590)    #[cfg(all(
[2591](https://docs.rs#2591)        feature = "std",

[2596](https://docs.rs#2596)            target_os = "wasi",

[2653](https://docs.rs#2653)    /// The corresponding `deserialize_internal` method sacrifices some invariant-checking

[2659](https://docs.rs#2659)    pub fn deserialize_internal<'de, D>(deserializer: D) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<Self, D::Error>

[2661](https://docs.rs#2661)        D: [serde::Deserializer](https://docs.rs/serde_core/1.0.228/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/serde_core/de/trait.Deserializer.html)<'de>,

[2676](https://docs.rs#2676)        let url = [Url](https://docs.rs#228-250) {

[2694](https://docs.rs#2694)    /// Assuming the URL is in the `file` scheme or similar,
[2695](https://docs.rs#2695)    /// convert its path to an absolute `std::path::Path`.
[2696](https://docs.rs#2696)    ///
[2697](https://docs.rs#2697)    /// **Note:** This does not actually check the URL’s `scheme`,
[2698](https://docs.rs#2698)    /// and may give nonsensical results for other schemes.
[2699](https://docs.rs#2699)    /// It is the user’s responsibility to check the URL’s scheme before calling this.
[2700](https://docs.rs#2700)    ///
[2701](https://docs.rs#2701)    /// ```
[2702](https://docs.rs#2702)    /// # use url::Url;
[2703](https://docs.rs#2703)    /// # let url = Url::parse("file:///etc/passwd").unwrap();
[2704](https://docs.rs#2704)    /// let path = url.to_file_path();
[2705](https://docs.rs#2705)    /// ```
[2706](https://docs.rs#2706)    ///
[2707](https://docs.rs#2707)    /// Returns `Err` if the host is neither empty nor `"localhost"` (except on Windows, where
[2708](https://docs.rs#2708)    /// `file:` URLs may have a non-local host),
[2709](https://docs.rs#2709)    /// or if `Path::new_opt()` returns `None`.
[2710](https://docs.rs#2710)    /// (That is, if the percent-decoded path contains a NUL byte or,
[2711](https://docs.rs#2711)    /// for a Windows path, is not UTF-8.)
[2712](https://docs.rs#2712)    ///
[2713](https://docs.rs#2713)    /// This method is only available if the `std` Cargo feature is enabled.
[2714](https://docs.rs#2714)    #[inline]
[2715](https://docs.rs#2715)    #[cfg(all(
[2716](https://docs.rs#2716)        feature = "std",
[2717](https://docs.rs#2717)        any(
[2718](https://docs.rs#2718)            unix,
[2719](https://docs.rs#2719)            windows,
[2720](https://docs.rs#2720)            target_os = "redox",
[2721](https://docs.rs#2721)            target_os = "wasi",
[2722](https://docs.rs#2722)            target_os = "hermit"
[2723](https://docs.rs#2723)        )
[2724](https://docs.rs#2724)    ))]
[2725](https://docs.rs#2725)    #[allow(clippy::result_unit_err)]
[2726](https://docs.rs#2726)    pub fn to_file_path(&self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[PathBuf](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/struct.PathBuf.html), ()> {
[2727](https://docs.rs#2727)        if let [Some](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.Some)(segments) = [self](https://docs.rs#2726).[path_segments](https://docs.rs#1442-1445)() {
[2728](https://docs.rs#2728)            let host = match [self](https://docs.rs#2726).[host](https://docs.rs#1201-1208)() {
[2729](https://docs.rs#2729)                [None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) | [Some](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.Some)(Host::[Domain](https://docs.rs/host.rs.html#51)("localhost")) => [None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None),
[2730](https://docs.rs#2730)                [Some](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.Some)(_) if [cfg!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/macro.cfg.html)(windows) && [self](https://docs.rs#2726).[scheme](https://docs.rs#903-905)() == "file" => {
[2731](https://docs.rs#2731)                    [Some](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.Some)(&[self](https://docs.rs#2726).serialization[self.host_start as usize..self.host_end as usize])
[2732](https://docs.rs#2732)                }
[2733](https://docs.rs#2733)                _ => return [Err](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html#variant.Err)(()),
[2734](https://docs.rs#2734)            };
[2735](https://docs.rs#2735)
[2736](https://docs.rs#2736)            let str_len = [self](https://docs.rs#2726).[as_str](https://docs.rs#653-655)().[len](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.str.html#method.len)();
[2737](https://docs.rs#2737)            let estimated_capacity = if [cfg!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/macro.cfg.html)(target_os = "redox") {
[2738](https://docs.rs#2738)                let scheme_len = [self](https://docs.rs#2726).[scheme](https://docs.rs#903-905)().[len](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.str.html#method.len)();
[2739](https://docs.rs#2739)                let file_scheme_len = "file".[len](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.str.html#method.len)();
[2740](https://docs.rs#2740)                // remove only // because it still has file:
[2741](https://docs.rs#2741)                if [scheme_len](https://docs.rs#2738) < [file_scheme_len](https://docs.rs#2739) {
[2742](https://docs.rs#2742)                    let scheme_diff = [file_scheme_len](https://docs.rs#2739) - [scheme_len](https://docs.rs#2738);
[2743](https://docs.rs#2743)                    ([str_len](https://docs.rs#2736) + [scheme_diff](https://docs.rs#2742)).[saturating_sub](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.usize.html#method.saturating_sub)(2)
[2744](https://docs.rs#2744)                } else {
[2745](https://docs.rs#2745)                    let scheme_diff = [scheme_len](https://docs.rs#2738) - [file_scheme_len](https://docs.rs#2739);
[2746](https://docs.rs#2746)                    [str_len](https://docs.rs#2736).[saturating_sub](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.usize.html#method.saturating_sub)([scheme_diff](https://docs.rs#2745) + 2)
[2747](https://docs.rs#2747)                }
[2748](https://docs.rs#2748)            } else if [cfg!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/macro.cfg.html)(windows) {
[2749](https://docs.rs#2749)                // remove scheme: - has possible \\ for hostname
[2750](https://docs.rs#2750)                [str_len](https://docs.rs#2736).[saturating_sub](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.usize.html#method.saturating_sub)([self](https://docs.rs#2726).[scheme](https://docs.rs#903-905)().[len](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.str.html#method.len)() + 1)
[2751](https://docs.rs#2751)            } else {
[2752](https://docs.rs#2752)                // remove scheme://
[2753](https://docs.rs#2753)                [str_len](https://docs.rs#2736).[saturating_sub](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.usize.html#method.saturating_sub)([self](https://docs.rs#2726).[scheme](https://docs.rs#903-905)().[len](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.str.html#method.len)() + 3)
[2754](https://docs.rs#2754)            };
[2755](https://docs.rs#2755)            return [file_url_segments_to_pathbuf](https://docs.rs#3064-3114)([estimated_capacity](https://docs.rs#2737), [host](https://docs.rs#2728), [segments](https://docs.rs#2727));
[2756](https://docs.rs#2756)        }
[2757](https://docs.rs#2757)        [Err](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html#variant.Err)(())
[2758](https://docs.rs#2758)    }

Parse an absolute URL from a string and add params to its query string.

Existing params are not removed.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-1)Examples

```
use url::Url;
let url = Url::parse_with_params("https://example.net?dont=clobberme",
                                 &[("lang", "rust"), ("browser", "servo")])?;
assert_eq!("https://example.net/?dont=clobberme&lang=rust&browser=servo", url.as_str());
```
[§](https://docs.rs#errors-1)Errors

If the function can not parse an absolute URL from the given string,
